title: Optimized immunofluorescence staining protocol for imaging germinal centers in secondary lymphoid tissues of vaccinated mice
protocol: Set up the cryostat as described in Materials and Equipment section.
Transport the OCT frozen tissue block in dry ice to a cryostat.
Allow the tissue block to reach cryostat chamber temperature for approximately 30 minutes.
Cut the OCT frozen tissue block to size using a razor blade.
Apply OCT to a specimen disc at 20°C–22°C and place the frozen tissue block on top.
Transfer the tissue block immediately to the quick freeze shelf inside the cryostat until completely frozen.
Cut sections according to the desired thickness.
Remove slides from −80°C.
Air-dry slides under airflow for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Draw an unbroken circle around tissue sections with a PAP pen.
Leave the slides for 15-30 minutes until the wax has completely dried.
Rehydrate slides by transferring them to a staining jar or dish.
Wash slides three times for 5 minutes with Wash Buffer at 20°C–22°C.
Maintain slides hydrated throughout the procedure using a humidified chamber during staining.
Add blocking buffer for 60–120 minutes at 20°C–22°C to minimize non-specific binding of primary and secondary antibodies.
Select an appropriate type of normal serum to prevent interactions with tissue or antibodies.
Wash slides three times for 5 minutes with Wash Buffer at 20°C–22°C.
Use a Streptavidin/Biotin Blocking Kit to block endogenous biotin.
Incubate each tissue section with streptavidin solution for 15 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse quickly with Wash Buffer solution.
Incubate for 15 minutes with the biotin solution at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse quickly with Wash Buffer solution twice.
Add Permeabilization buffer and incubate for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Wash slides with Wash Buffer three times for 5 minutes each at 20°C–22°C.
Prepare primary antibody dilutions.
Pipette the primary antibody mix onto the slide, ensuring complete coverage of each section.
Incubate the covered slide in a dark humidified chamber for 60–120 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Include controls such as minus primary antibody, secondary antibody alone and/or isotypes control.
Wash slides with Wash Buffer three times for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C to remove unbound antibodies.
Prepare secondary antibody dilutions in antibody diluent (2% Normal Goat serum in Wash Buffer solution).
Pipette the secondary antibody mix onto the slide, ensuring each section is completely covered.
Incubate the slide in a dark humidified chamber for 60–120 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse slides two times with Wash Buffer quickly.
Pour off the Wash Buffer and rinse with 1×PBS quickly.
Wipe off excess 1×PBS without disrupting the tissue.
Mount the tissue with mounting medium, adding a drop directly onto the tissue and gently placing coverslip on top to avoid bubbles.
Dry slides at 20°C–22°C until the mounting medium has set.
Store dried slides at 4°C for imaging.
Place the microscope slide onto the stage of the microscope ensuring the coverslip is facing the objective lens.
Select a high Numerical Aperture (NA) plan apochromatic air objective, e.g., 20× 0.8 NA Plan Apo.
Position the tissue section directly in front of the objective lens using the stage x/y controller.
Mark the location of the tissue section on the slide if it is very thin.
Select an appropriate filter set to observe the sample by eye in Zen software, e.g., “FITC”.
Check that light is coming out of the objective lens.
Look down the eyepieces to focus the sample and position to a region of interest.
Configure scanning parameters in the Acquisition Mode window.
Set a 1024×1024 scan at 1× zoom with a pixel size of 0.42 μm using a 20× 0.8 NA lens.
Set Scan Mode to Frame, Line Step to 1, Speed to 7–10, and Averaging to 1, 2 or 4 based on signal strength.
Set Mode to Line, Method to Mean, Bit Depth to 8 bit, and Direction to <-> for bi-direction scanning.
Deselect one Track in the active Track, ensuring only one detector is active.
Start scanning using the “Live” button.
Adjust fine focus on the microscope for strongest signal.
Set each of the Channels to 2% laser power, Gain (Master) to 700, Digital Offset to 0, and Digital Gain to 1 as an approximate starting configuration.
Adjust the laser power and/or Gain (Master) to give a bright image without saturation.
Keep the laser power below ~5% to prevent bleaching.
Maintain the Gain (Master) below ~750 to minimize noise.
Adjust the Digital Offset to maximize contrast in the image, avoiding zero value pixels.
Repeat this process for all detectors in all tracks.
Ensure all detectors and tracks are turned on.
Acquire images using the "Snap" button.
